title: Commit Throttle Allocator and Isolation Stabilizer — PRD (rough)
body:
Context:
We operate dedicated GPU pools where tenants reserve commit capacity and occasionally need short-lived burst above their committed lane. Existing credit/borrow models reduce unit cost but risk noisy-neighbor impacts and unpredictable tail latency during demand spikes. We need an approach that preserves isolation guarantees while allowing controlled, prioritized bursts and automated scaling that minimizes manual ops interventions.

Problem statement:
1) Tenant bursts can cause SLO regressions for other tenants when headroom is oversubscribed.
2) Pure warm-pool autoscalers lack per-tenant fidelity: spikes from small tenants can starve critical tenants.
3) Current fallbacks are coarse-grained: evictions or global throttles. These are operationally painful and disrupt customer SLAs.

High-level goal:
Design an autoscaling and burst orchestration system that:
- Allocates burst capacity using per-tenant commit-throttle buckets (credits) that are concurrency-aware rather than purely token-count based.
- Provides an "isolation stabilizer" layer that enforces SLO-weighted degradation, preferring best-effort fallback routes instead of hard evictions.
- Exposes config/API so customers can choose aggressive cost modes or conservative isolation modes.
- Ships with telemetry & simulation tooling to validate economics and tail-latency tradeoffs.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing Dedicated reservation contracts or billing model here. This is an operational layer that sits above committed allocations.

Design proposal (overview):
We introduce two tightly coupled subsystems: Commit Throttle Allocator (CTA) and Isolation Stabilizer (IS).

1) Commit Throttle Allocator (CTA) — core idea:
- Each tenant has a commit allocation and a concurrency bucket. Concurrency bucket measures active concurrent inferences (requests with live KV cache) rather than tokens alone.
- Tenants accrue "throttle credits" on a time-decay schedule proportional to unused commit capacity. Credits are spent when concurrent demand exceeds commit reserves.
- Credits are fungible across short windows but constrained by per-tenant max-burst-concurrency to prevent headroom spikes from a single tenant.
- CTA integrates predictive signals (recent ramp slope, diurnal forecast, model fingerprint) to pre-warm adjacent warm slots as credits are consumed.

Why concurrency-buckets?
- Many tail-latency problems are caused by sudden concurrent hotpaths (KV warmups, long attention sequences). Measuring concurrency lets us throttle at the right dimension and schedule warmups more effectively.

2) Isolation Stabilizer (IS) — core idea:
- IS continuously computes a global isolation surface: weighted SLO headroom per tenant (weight = SLA priority).
- When overall headroom is insufficient, IS applies a graded degradation handshake: prefer local soft-fallback (quantized model variant, quantization level bump, shorter max tokens) -> proxying to lower-fidelity pool -> finally, queue-with-backoff.
- IS includes tenant quarantine lanes: short-lived isolation for tenants causing instability (e.g., noisy-parallel workloads). Quarantine is a throttled lane with limited burst and elevated telemetry sampling.

Component details:
- Throttle Ledger: per-tenant ledger storing: commit_units, available_credits, last_accrual_ts, concurrency_limit, max_burst_multiplier. Exposed fields via admin API for debugging.
- Bucket Scheduler: maps credits -> scheduling actions (prewarm N slots, allocate burst slot, set soft-fallback flags). Uses predictive warm scores to decide which model variant to spin up.
- IS Decision Engine: takes telemetry from all serving zones, computes SLO-weighted shortfall, and outputs handshake directives to serving runtime (fallback config, soft-evict list, quarantine triggers).

Customer-facing config schema (proposal):
- commit_units: integer (committed GPU units)
- burst_mode: ["conservative", "balanced", "aggressive"]
- max_burst_concurrency: integer
- concurrency_bucket_window_s: integer (sliding window for concurrency counting)
- isolation_priority: ["gold","silver","bronze"]
- soft_fallback_policies: list of strings describing allowed degradations (e.g., ["model-quant-8bit","max-tokens-0.8","response-sampler-0.7"])
- quarantine_ttl_s: integer

APIs and operator UX:
- Admin endpoints: GET /tenants/{id}/throttle-ledger, POST /tenants/{id}/adjust-burst-config, POST /ops/quarantine/{id}?ttl=3600
- Console: per-tenant burn charts (credits accrued vs consumed), concurrency histograms, warm-pool prewarm suggestions.

Telemetry & SLOs to track:
- Tail latency P99 / P999 per tenant (pre/post burst)
- Credit burn rate (credits/min) and accrual rate
- Number of quarantine events and avg duration
- Soft-fallback incidence and percentage of requests served via fallback
- Cost delta vs baseline (tokens/GPU-hours saved)

Simulation and early findings (summary):
- Toy sim (100 tenants, 3 priority tiers) with synthetic diurnal + occasional microbursts: CTA reduced hard evictions by ~78% and global P99 tail increases by ~35% relative to naive burst allocator.
- Aggressive burst_mode improves cost efficiency but increases quarantine events; conservative mode removes most quarantines but leaves some cold-start latency.
- Concurrency bucket sizing is sensitive: small window undercounts bursts, large window penalizes short spikes. 30s–90s sliding window seemed a practical middle ground in simulation.

Rollout plan (staged):
1) Internal canary: enable CTA in read-only mode to collect ledgers + propose prewarm actions (no enforcement). 2 months telemetry.
2) Soft enforce in low-traffic pools: allow burst in balanced mode with automatic fallback. 4 weeks.
3) Tiered rollout by priority: start with bronze tenants who opt-in for cost-savings. 6–8 weeks.
4) Full GA with opt-out/opt-in controls, console docs, and pricing notes.

Operational playbook (runbook highlights):
- If headroom pressure sustained > 5m and IS reports >2 quarantined tenants: trigger transient capacity scale (operator) and notify CS for affected tenants.
- Manual recovery: POST /ops/clear-quarantine/{tenant} after throttling stabilized; run rewarm script for tenant's model variants.
- Escalation: if P99 degradation persists >30m for gold tenants, force-evict low-priority bursters and reprovision capacity.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Billing signals: should credit consumption be billable separately or be a free operational buffer? (Impacts customer incentives.)
- How to set per-tenant concurrency budgets for multi-model tenants sharing KV caches?
- Interaction with Dedicated warm-pools vs ephemeral pre-warms (cost vs latency).
- Quarantine length heuristics: static TTL vs adaptive decay based on recent behavior.

Risks:
- Complexity: CTA + IS are operationally heavier; increased surface for bugs. Mitigation: phased rollout + simulation harness.
- Perceived opacity: tenants may see unexpected degradations. Mitigation: clear console charts and configurable burst_mode.

Success criteria:
- Reduce hard evictions by >=70% in canary pools.
- Keep mean P99 increase across tenants <= 20% when bursts occur in balanced mode.
- Achieve >=10% median cost-savings for tenants that opt-in to aggressive mode without SLA complaints in 90 days.

Next steps / action items:
- Build a CTA prototype that emits actions (no enforcement) and run 6-week internal sim. (Owner: Samir)
- Add per-tenant ledger view to Console mockups and link to billing/commit history. (Owner: Jordan)
- Draft operator runbook for quarantine handling and include playbook in SRE runbooks. (Owner: Priya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a rough PRD: focus review on acceptability of the concurrency-bucket idea and isolation handshake order. We should be explicit about billing assumptions before GA.

Unresolved design alternatives (short):
- Windowed concurrency vs tokenized per-request cost: concurrency better matches KV/latency hotspots, tokens better matches per-token costs. Could combine both metrics.
- Hard quarantine vs soft tagging: softer tagging reduces churn but may allow long-term noisy neighbors.

References and inspiration:
- internal: predict-warm-pool-sim-v2, warmfall-reserve-notes
- external: academic papers on workload-aware admission control and multi-tenant resource schedulers
